ZH.Who — Round 4, From Scratch

Started over, outside Google Fonts. The first three rounds all failed for one reason: they were restricted to open-licence fonts, and the type this brief needs was made in the early 2000s by Ray Larabie, Iconian and ShyFoundry and given away as freeware. None of it is in that catalogue. The single most useful find: Larabie and Iconian share a variant scheme — expand adds width, ital adds lean, and half/laser cut horizontal slices clean through the strokes. Combined, those mechanically reproduce four of the six traits of the real UNDERGROUND lettering. Worth knowing: every canonical reference here — the Cyberpunk 2077 logo and its UI, the Blade Runner titles, Akira, Ghost in the Shell, and NFSU2's own UNDERGROUND band — is custom lettering, not a font. No typeface will ever be an exact match, which is the argument for drawing our own. These are ideas, not licence-cleared assets. Fifteen, not twenty: several candidates were cut rather than padded in.

01

Underground Band

Font
Bummer Half Regular Italic
Tracking
natural
Licence
Freeware / personal-use — not cleared for merch

The closest thing to the real UNDERGROUND lettering I have found: sheared terminals, chamfered joins, slit counters, a ~15° lean — and horizontal slices cut clean through every stroke, which is the detail no other face reproduces. Five of the six target traits in one cut.

Small-size risk: Unicase, so it sets @ZH.WHO and the toggles do nothing. Slices need size to survive.

The condensed extreme, at H-aspect 0.50 — half the width of a normal cap. Broken counters and LED-channel construction. Included because the brief's trait test is wide or narrow, never the middle, and this is the only true narrow.

Small-size risk: Its lowercase is 0.87 of cap, so the toggles barely register.

Production files are in this folder as NN-slug.svg. They are plain outlined SVG — open in Illustrator, Inkscape, Affinity or Cricut Design Space, or hand them to a printer as-is. Each file holds exactly two paths, one gold and one red, so colour separation is already done.

The keyline toggle previews a bone-coloured sticker border. Most print shops generate the actual die-cut contour themselves from the artwork outline, so send the flat files unless yours asks for a cut path.
